title: Prompt socket drift log
content:
Notes to self - evolving thinking about socket/streaming-induced prompt drift and a small few-shot library to repro and triage failures.

Context:
- Working on examples for the DX samples repo where we demo streaming responses over websocket-like connections. Several customers reported odd behavior when clients reconnect mid-generation or when partial tokens are processed locally and then resent as context.
- This doc is a messy scratchpad: hypotheses, small repro prompts, observed failure modes, quick mitigation ideas, and test ideas for the QA harness.

High-level observation (problem statement):
- When using streaming sockets + local buffering of partial output, the combination of re-sent context + incremental token appends causes the model to behave as if earlier instructions changed or were contradicted ("drift"). This is worse when:
  * few-shot examples are near the context window boundary, or
  * client-side dedup/glue logic concatenates partial outputs back into the prompt, or
  * reconnection happens and user adds a small clarifying prompt mid-stream.

Examples / minimal repro prompts: (use with hosted-demo environment, stream=true)

1) "echo-safety" quick repro (shows repetition + hallucinated role change):
- System: You are a concise assistant for summarization. Always label source sentences.
- Few-shot example A:
  Q: Summarize paragraph.
  A: [S1] ...
- User prompt: "Summarize the text below: \nText: 'The cat sat on the mat. It was blue.'"
- Behavior: On reconnect, the socket client resends 'Summarize the text below:' plus whatever partial tokens it received. The model output repeats labels and starts adding an invented policy statement at the top: "Policy: be concise" even though system said only label sentences.

2) "role-swap after partial" - shows role confusion:
- Few-shot examples: two Q/A pairs that set a pattern (question->answer). Mid-generation, client reconnects and appends a tiny clarifier: "Also be a lawyer."
- Observed: model starts inserting legal-style preamble and reinterprets previous examples as now being in that role.

Failure modes catalog (ranked by frequency):
- FM1: Repetition loop due to partial resend of trailing tokens (common).
- FM2: Role drift / sudden style shift when ephemeral clarifier is injected (common).
- FM3: Hallucinated constraints added (e.g., model invents new rules) after reconnect (less common).
- FM4: Truncation artifacts when few-shot examples are cut mid-example: results degrade unpredictably.
- FM5: Tokenization boundary artifacts - client-side split causes strange Unicode escapes or duplicate punctuation (rare but nasty).

Hypotheses (why this happens):
- The model uses the whole sequence distribution: even small appended clarifiers can reweight beam choices, especially when few-shot examples are highly informative.
- Partial tokens/partial completions when re-inserted look like new instructions, not continuations, because of missing separators (e.g., no \n\n or role token).
- Streaming clients with naive merging create duplicated instruction fragments which the model treats as reinforcement of a (possibly contradictory) instruction set.

Mitigations (quick experiments to try):
- Client-side canonicalization: ensure every resumed prompt uses explicit separators and role markers. E.g., always insert "\n--REPLY RESUMED--\n" before re-appending partial tokens.
- Use generation metadata: if backend can mark token positions as "partial" vs "committed", expose that in socket protocol and avoid resending committed tokens.
- Template-level guardrails: in top-level system message add an explicit instruction: "Ignore repeated fragments that are identical to what you already saw; treat bracketed 'RESUME' markers as not new instructions." Test if this reduces hallucinated policies.
- Few-shot placement: move examples to earlier in the context and place an explicit separator after them; or use a canonical 'example bank' stored externally and referenced by id (not pasted) when possible.

Quick few-shot templates to test (distinct flavors):
- TEMPLATE A (instruction-first):
  [system] You are a faithful summarizer. Do not infer beyond the text.
  [examples]
  EX1-Q: ...
  EX1-A: ...
  [user] Summarize: <TEXT>
- TEMPLATE B (format-first):
  [system] Output MUST start with: "SUMMARY:" and then bullet points.
  [fewshot examples formatted as exact output-match]
- TEMPLATE C (resilience-primed):
  [system] If you see a marker "<RESUME>", treat it as metadata and ignore it for instruction extraction.

Small test matrix (variables):
- streaming: true/false
- partial-resend: none/minimal/full
- fewshot placement: head/middle/tail
- separator: explicit (\n) vs none vs token marker
- clarifier injection: present/absent

Telemetry metrics to add (observable signals):
- rate of unique instruction tokens that appear after reconnect relative to before reconnect (proxy for drift).
- repetition score (n-gram overlap between successive streaming chunks).
- style divergence metric (BLEU/style embedding shift) between first chunk and later chunks.
- percent of completions that contain words like "policy", "rules", "must" that didn't appear in initial system prompt.

Hypothesis-driven experiments (quick runs):
- H1: Adding a RESUME marker reduces FM1/FM3 by ~40% (A/B test).
- H2: Moving few-shot examples to the start reduces role drift cases when reconnects happen late.
- H3: System message explicit "ignore duplicates" reduces hallucinated new constraints.

Notes from last demo w/ QA (2026-02-14):
- QA team reproduced repeated labels when fewshot example boarder was at 3/4 context. Diego suggests we add a small checksum: when client reconnects, include last committed token id (opaque) so server can detect duplicate insertion.
- Priya pointed out that in some languages (Japanese) tokenization boundaries make the problem worse; add language dimension to test matrix.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add RESUME marker option to socket sample client (Maya).
- [ ] Add 'ignore duplicate fragments' variant to demo templates (Diego).
- [ ] Add telemetry events for reconnections and post-reconnect instruction tokens (SRE/Observability ticket).
- [ ] Create a small test harness that simulates reconnects at random offsets (QA).
- [ ] Draft short internal note on "best practices for streaming clients" to be published in DX repo (target: next week).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is it feasible to implement per-token commit markers at scale without adding too much overhead to runtime? (perf tradeoff with RPCs)
- How many customers are changing the client-side behavior vs using our SDKs (we should prioritize SDK fixes if majority use them).
- Could a model-level prompt-engineering pattern (e.g., 'context bank by id') be productized so we don't paste examples?

Random scratch examples (do not use in production):
- "You are an assistant. If you see <RESUME> ignore it. Answer: <user text>"
- Few-shot pair (short): Q: Who won the match? A: Use facts only.

Footer: this is rough. Save iterations here. When we stabilize a small reproducible test case, move to 'dx/examples/streaming-reconnect-tests' and link PR.
